title: Joel
summary: Joel is a biblical book focused on the day of the Lord, repentance, Spirit, and restoration.
historical_context: Joel moves from communal crisis to repentance, restoration, and the promise of the poured-out Spirit.
ancient_near_east_context: Joel belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Joel should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Joel as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Minor Prophets, book 2 of 12, Joel contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting the day of the Lord, repentance, Spirit, and restoration to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Joel as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Joel uses prophecy, poetry within Minor Prophets, book 2 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Joel helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars recognize collection and editorial shaping
date_ranges: 8th-5th centuries BCE, depending on the prophet
Final forms often reflect later collection and editing
original_audience: Israel and Judah under covenant accountability before and after exile
historical_setting: Assyrian, Babylonian, and post-exilic settings across the prophetic corpus
canonical_role: Joel anchors the day of the Lord, repentance, Spirit, and restoration within Minor Prophets, book 2 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
structure: Day of the LORD and Spirit promise
interpretive_disputes: How to read prophetic poetry, irony, and symbolic action

related_objects.notes: The day of the Lord is the book's central prophetic horizon.
The book calls the community to return to the Lord.
Judgment gives way to restoration hope.
The promise of poured-out Spirit is central to later canonical use.
Judgment language shapes the book's crisis and hope.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Joel first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
The relationship links on Joel are orientation anchors, not a full interpretive outline of the book.
